metadata.title: US crypto-regulation state tracker (Sep 2026): SEC 'Project Crypto'/Regulation Crypto Assets, the CFTC 'Crypto Sprint', SEC-CFTC harmonization, bank-regulator deregulation, and the live CLARITY Act
metadata.frame: A snapshot of the AFFIRMATIVE US regulatory posture on crypto as of Sep 2026 - distinct from the enforcement-actor map and the CLARITY delay chronology. Two agency programs are converging: the SEC's 'Project Crypto' (Chair Atkins) -> a March-17-2026 SEC/CFTC joint interpretive release + five-category token taxonomy -> the 'Regulation Crypto Assets' / Innovation-Exemption rulemaking (at OIRA since Apr 6 2026); and the CFTC's 12-month 'Crypto Sprint' (launched Aug 2025) implementing the President's Working Group report - listed spot crypto (Bitnomial, Dec 4 2025), a tokenized-collateral pilot (payment stablecoins/BTC/ETH as margin, Dec 8 2025 no-action), and a blockchain-market-infra rulemaking targeted for completion Aug 2026. In parallel the prudential bank regulators (OCC, Fed, FDIC) rolled back Biden-era crypto restrictions. Statute (CLARITY) remains the durability backstop and is stalled at a Sep-15-2026 Senate cloture vote.
metadata.grade: Agency actions, dates, personnel, and the taxonomy/exemption/sprint pillars = FACT (SEC.gov statements; CFTC press releases; OCC interpretive letters; law-firm analyses Sidley/Greenberg Traurig/Morgan Lewis/WilmerHale/King & Spalding). The CLARITY cloture date and 60-vote hurdle = FACT; whether it passes in 2026 = OPEN/doubtful (prediction markets cut odds). 'Durable protection needs Congress' is Atkins's stated position; the single-commissioner-CFTC durability concern is an analyst INTERPRETATION.
metadata.honest_limits: Proposed SEC rules are NOT final - 'Regulation Crypto Assets' is at OIRA pre-publication, not adopted, and structural legal challenges to the safe-harbor's authority are already being prepared. No-action relief and interpretive letters are agency positions that a future administration can withdraw (as the Fed did to Biden-era guidance) - which is precisely why Atkins frames CLARITY as necessary. This block tracks POSTURE and PROCESS, not settled law.
metadata.method: SEC.gov (Atkins 'Project Crypto' 111225; 'Regulation Crypto Assets' 081826; Mar-17-2026 interpretive release); CFTC press releases 9105/9109/9145/9146/9150-25 + Selig bio; Sep-2-2025 SEC/CFTC joint spot statement; OCC Interpretive Letter 1186 + riskless-principal guidance; Fed/FDIC deregulation notes; CLARITY status via CoinDesk/CNBC/CryptoSlate/Latham tracker (Aug-Sep 2026).

edges.notes: SEC Chair Paul Atkins's flagship digital-asset program (unveiled 2025; 'inside Project Crypto' speech Nov-12-2025) to modernize securities rules for crypto and 'restore American leadership' - a Chair driving rulemaking through the formal process rather than a policy statement (fact).

The rulemaking package: Atkins previewed 'Regulation Crypto Assets' (statement Aug-18-2026); at OIRA pre-publication review since Apr-6-2026, could publish as an NPRM any day. OIRA (Sep-4-2025) flagged two 2026 proposals - a comprehensive crypto-asset framework and Exchange-Act amendments for crypto trading on exchanges/ATSs. NOT final (fact of process; adoption pending - graded).

Three pillars (announced Mar-17-2026): Startup Exemption (early raises capped ~$5M over 4 yrs); Fundraising Exemption (mid-scale capped ~$75M per 12 mo); and an Investment-Contract Safe Harbor letting a token transition security->non-security when the issuer's essential managerial efforts cease (a status test, not the earlier 3-year clock). Legal-authority challenges already being prepared (fact of framework; durability contested).
edges.source: #215 crypto-reg tracker (SEC.gov Mar-2026 release; KuCoin guide; Astraea)

edges.notes: The two agencies are actively harmonizing: Sep-2-2025 joint statement (current law doesn't bar a CFTC-registered DCM from listing certain spot digital assets); Mar-17-2026 JOINT interpretive release on Howey + a five-category token taxonomy (an objective anchor for the cessation test); Jan-29-2026 Selig+Atkins joint plans to make the US 'the world's crypto capital' (fact).
edges.source: #215 crypto-reg tracker (SEC/CFTC joint statement; Steptoe; Reed Smith)

edges.notes: A 12-month program launched Aug-2025 (under then-Acting Chair Caroline Pham) implementing the President's Working Group on Digital Asset Markets report; targeted to complete ~Aug-2026. Michael Selig (ex-chief counsel of the SEC Crypto Task Force, Atkins advisor) confirmed CFTC Chair Dec-18-2025, sworn Dec-22-2025 (term to Apr-2029); Pham then resigned (joined MoonPay), leaving a SINGLE commissioner - fast decisions but a bipartisan-balance/durability concern senators flag for 2026 (fact + analyst interpretation).

Pillar 1: spot crypto contracts listed on CFTC-registered futures exchanges (DCMs). First leveraged spot product went live on Bitnomial Exchange (announced Dec-4-2025) - the first spot crypto on a CFTC-regulated venue (fact).

Pillar 2: Dec-8-2025 Market Participants Division no-action relief + a 3-month Pilot Program letting FCMs accept non-securities digital assets as margin collateral - initially only PAYMENT STABLECOINS, BTC, and ETH (plus tokenized money-market funds); DCOs targeted to go live Q1-Q2 2026. Pillar 3 (blockchain-infra technical rulemaking on collateral/margin/clearing/settlement/reporting) targeted for completion Aug-2026 (fact).

Payment stablecoins (as defined under the GENIUS Act regime) are the lead eligible collateral in the CFTC pilot - a concrete on-ramp tying the stablecoin statute to derivatives-market plumbing (fact).

OCC Interpretive Letter 1186 (late-2025/early-2026): national banks may hold small amounts of crypto to pay blockchain 'gas' fees and to test DLT ('convenient or useful' / incidental to banking); separate guidance permits 'riskless principal' crypto transactions (matching customer buy/sell without inventory) with strong BSA/AML + governance controls. Technology-neutral, risk-based (fact).
edges.source: #215 crypto-reg tracker (OCC IL 1186; Goodwin; King & Spalding; Elliptic)

edges.notes: Part of the coordinated prudential rollback: the Fed withdrew Biden-era bank-crypto supervisory guidance; the OCC removed 'reputation risk' from exam criteria - lowering the supervisory friction that had kept banks out of crypto (fact of actions).
edges.source: #215 crypto-reg tracker (Fed withdrawal; King & Spalding roundup)

edges.notes: FDIC clarified that supervised banks do NOT need prior approval to engage in crypto activities - reversing the prior de-facto pause and completing the tri-regulator (OCC/Fed/FDIC) green light (fact).

The statutory backstop, STALLED: House passed 294-134 (Jul-2025); Senate Banking advanced 15-9 (May-2026); Majority Leader Thune filed cloture Aug-8-2026; a procedural cloture / motion-to-proceed vote (needs 60, i.e. Democratic votes) is set for Sep-15-2026 - NOT final passage. Prediction markets cut 2026-enactment odds; many view it as 'dead in 2026' pending sticking points (fact of schedule; outcome open).
edges.source: #215 crypto-reg tracker (CoinDesk 2026-08-08; CNBC 2026-09-01; CryptoSlate; Latham tracker)

edges.notes: CLARITY would statutorily divide SEC/CFTC authority over digital assets (securities vs digital commodities) - codifying, and making durable, the administrative posture the two agencies are building via Project Crypto + the Crypto Sprint (fact of bill design).

The digital-commodity spot-market authority CLARITY would give the CFTC is the statutory version of what the Crypto Sprint is doing administratively (listed spot on DCMs) - the SEC-vs-CFTC two-committee split is itself one of the delay factors (fact/interpretation).

Atkins's stated position: rules alone aren't enough - legislation is 'indispensable' to 'future-proof' the framework against a 'future rogue regulator' unwinding it; the SEC 'has and will continue to support Congress in delivering the CLARITY Act.' The administrative buildout is explicitly framed as needing the statute for durability (fact of stated position).

The already-enacted GENIUS Act (payment-stablecoin regime) is the statutory foundation the CFTC leans on to admit payment stablecoins as margin - the one piece of the crypto statutory stack that DID pass, in contrast to the stalled CLARITY market-structure bill (fact).
